root_cause.text: The log roundoff value `l_iclog_roundoff` was incorrectly set to a hardcoded 512 bytes (BBSIZE) when no log stripe unit was specified in the superblock, ignoring the actual log sector size (`sb_logsectsize`), causing misalignment and corruption on filesystems with larger sector sizes (e.g., 4K).
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an `else if` branch to use `mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize` when `sb_logsunit` is not available, instead of always falling back to `BBSIZE`. The CVE description confirms that on a disk with log sectsz=4096 and sunit=0, the roundoff factor was 512, leading to torn writes and mount failures.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix iclog roundoff assignment to properly use the log sector size when log version 2 is not enabled or logsunit is not specified.
intent_record.what: Added an else-if branch in xlog_alloc_log to set l_iclog_roundoff to sb_logsectsize if it is greater than 0, when the previous condition (logv2 and logsunit > 1) is false.
intent_record.how: This change modifies the iclog roundoff assignment to prefer the log sector size from the superblock (if positive) over the default BBSIZE, when the log version 2 feature or its unit size is not applicable. This affects the alignment of iclogs during log initialization.

grouping_result.intent: Fix iclog roundoff assignment to properly use the log sector size when log version 2 is not enabled or logsunit is not specified.

relevance_review.reason: The group's core intent directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by fixing the iclog roundoff assignment to use the proper log sector size instead of a hardcoded 512 bytes.

candidates.rationale: This statement assigns a hardcoded BBSIZE (512 bytes) as the iclog roundoff value, ignoring the log sector size (sb_logsectsize). When the filesystem uses a larger sector size (e.g., 4K), this causes misalignment and corruption.
